comment: The Gold Wiener Gala is almost over and host Al "Corny" Caprice is about to crack tonight's last joke, when <¤Cband.name> charge on stage.\n\t<¤CRealMusicianDrums.Name> is riding on Roy Dowert's back and catches "Corny" with a tablecloth lasso.\n\tThey conquer the mic and declare to the world, "Music and love make the world go round!" before security remove them from the stage.

<¤Cband.name> are nominated for a Gold Wiener in the Intricate Singing-category.\n\tThe Gold Wiener is the music industry's yearly award ceremony in which prominent artists and businesses are credited for contributing to the progress of the music business.\n\tWinning a Gold Wiener is highly regarded.

Champagne corks pop as award presenter Billy Mutton announces the winner in the Intricate Singing-category. <¤Cband.name> win the Gold Wiener!\n\tThey celebrate by spraying each other with champagne and throwing canapés at the trade minister.

No Gold Wiener for <¤Cband.name> this time around.\n\tThe prize for Intricate Singing was awarded to The M.A.C.K for the song Steamy Lovin', a crap tune according to your band.\n\tBut the band doesn't appear to be too disappointed, busy as they are filling mouths and pockets with free beer and food from the buffet.

The music makes the under-stimulated orphanage kids go berserk.\n\tIn a matter of minutes, they've destroyed all your gear and most of the orphanage's furniture.\n\tYou are curtly sent away by the headmistress.
The staff are touched by the beautiful concert and by your concern for the poor orphans.\n\tThe poor orphans themselves seem more interested in bullying a fat kid than listening to your music.
The record label want you to do a PR-gig at an orphanage.\n\tWhen Lucy Birch hears about it, she bursts out crying. It turns out that she's an orphan herself and she insists you do the gig.
Your funds are limited so spend them carefully. You may try again and make sure to do better this time.
You're broke. The game is over. <¤Cband.name> decide to give up. Now they'll return to their day jobs in various record shops.
<¤Crealmusician.name>'s leaving the band has made the rest of <¤cband.name> doubt whether this really is the right thing for them.\n\tAll worry except Lucy, who doesn't seem to care.

As a leftover from the past "space" concept days, <¤cband.name> have kept the band mascot  a "space" hamster called Ugly.
	The poor rodent's life ended tragically today when Lucy accidentally stepped on him , puncturing him with her stiletto heel.
	The band is shaken and some see it as a bad omen.
	Lucy herself doesn't seem to care much about Ugly's passing, pointing out that "one can always buy a new rat should the need occur."

City News critic Douglas Marvel seems to consider <¤Calbum.name> a personal insult.\n\t"A spit in the face of those serious about music. Anyone involved in the recording or distribution of this stinking rat's carcass of a record ought to be shot for crimes against humanity.\n\t"I've come to realise if the Devil does indeed exist, he comes in the shape of <¤Cband.name>. From this moment on, I promise to dedicate all of my effort as a music journalist to ending the curse, the horror, the abomination that is <¤Cband.name>."

Madman Douglas Marvel delivers another slap of abuse in today's City News:
	"<¤Calbum.name> is so bad, it leaves me no rest. I can't stop listening and the more I listen, the more I hate it.
	"Someone please help me stop this nightmare! Hurt me! Torture me! Put needles under my fingernails and set my hair on fire! Do whatever you need to stop me from listening to the painful sounds of <¤Cband.name>.
	"It's them or me as we cannot co-exist. If you're not part of the solution, you're part of the problem!"

There's a knock on the door of the practice room and you're surprised to find raving lunatic Douglas Marvel outside, hair on end, carrying a huge sign saying "Stop <¤Cband.name>!"\n\tHe wants to tell the band in person how he feels about the music they make. He humbly asks them to find other means of supporting themselves than through music.\n\tThen he leaves as suddenly as he came.

Marty feels real awkward about how the media in general and Douglas Marvel in particular have been acting toward <¤Cband.name>.\n\tHe is beginning to feel that being in a band may not be worth it.\n\tMarty is considering leaving music to pursue a career as a bus boy.

Last night, Lucy Birch ran into a well loaded Douglas Marvel in the popular night club Mirror Ball.
	<¤Cband.name>'s sworn enemy immediately came on to her, but Lucy politely resisted Marvel's driveling persuasions.
	When he started groping for her bosom, Lucy made security escort him out of her sight.
	Lucy doesn't appear disturbed by the incident.

Radio FM reporter Lola Hertz gets wind of Marvel's behaviour toward Lucy Birch and is furious.\n\tApparently he met ms. Hertz on the very same evening and told her she had bad taste in music.\n\tLola offers to do a live debate with <¤Cband.name> versus Douglas Marvel on the radio as an attempt to put an end to the madness.

<¤Cband.name> are not able to articulate themselves during the broadcasted debate.\n\tAny attempt they make to counter the verbal onslaught falls short compared to the rhetorical whirlwind that is Douglas Marvel.\n\tWhen the one hour debate is over, Marvel has convinced even Lola Hertz that <¤Cband.name> is a menace to society and should be treated accordingly.

The radio debate becomes <¤Cband.name>'s finest hour.
	Douglas Marvel stutters incoherently for a few minutes before he shuts up completely, leaving the airwaves to <¤Cband.name>.
	The band puts Marvel's outrage into perspective with an open-hearted account of how although their music may not be the most original ever to be put on a record, it is still the work of passion and honesty.
	Later, you are informed that Marvel has taken a long leave of absence from his position with City News.

Following the radio debate, Zer0 Magazine prints a <¤Calbum.name> review full of praise.\n\tThey call the record "a statement against narrow-mindedness and musical elitism" and add an insightful remark stating how they as critics often are too quick to dismiss aspiring artists as talentless one-hit-wonders.

Zer0 Magazine prints a review that sides with Douglas Marvel.\n\t"<¤Cband.name> is to the 21st century what the Black Death was to the Dark Ages. On Sunday, Zer0 Magazine will arrange a public burning of <¤Calbum.name> in Rock City Main Square.\n\t"Show up and burn your copy!"
Roy Dowert just makes it when a huge stack of amplifiers fall on stage.\n\tThe band keeps playing but the sound is a bit strange.

In the middle of the set, Roy Dowert has an inspired moment and tries to climb the light rig.\n\tRoy climbs very high  before he falls! He falls and breaks his arm (and the show).\n\tNow he'll have to lay low for a few days.

During the intro for the first song, Roy walks up to the front of the stage to greet the crowd. Unfortunately he trips on some cables, falls from the stage and breaks his foot.\n\tThe roadies pull him backstage while the band continues to play the intro for a few minutes more. Soon they give up and leave while the crowd boos.\n\tRoy has to wear a cast for a few weeks.

The show is interrupted by the police charging onto the stage arresting Roy Dowert.\n\tHe exposed himself on stage, which was the only excuse the police needed to arrest him.\n\tRoy is released a few hours later, fully dressed and without legal consequences.

Halfway through the show Roy Dowert gets some feeling and jumps into the crowd.\n\tA roadie runs out and starts pulling the microphone cable back. He gets the mic, but no Roy.\n\tThe band keeps playing for a while, before they stop and go backstage. The audience boos, but Roy is nowhere to be found.

Roy's mysterious disappearance  troubles the band members.\n\tThey worry about him, place phone calls to his friends asking his whereabouts, and generally do what worried people do.\n\tLucy Birch  on the other hand  only shrugs, like Roy will be back when he is ready.

Having been gone for three full days, Roy Dowert walks in to the practice room still in his stage costume.\n\tHe says he doesn't remember clearly what happened, but some kind girls drove him home.\n\tThey drove for about three hours, which is a tad strange considering <getObjByID(missionvar.roydisappearplaceID).name> is three blocks from the practice room.
<¤Cband.name> do a scandal by going on stage nude for the encore. The crowd love it and it's a field day for the photographers.
Your poor handling of the media became the end of <¤Cband.name>.\n\tTry again, and this time try to maintain a good relation to the ladies and gentlemen of the press.

The media's declaration of war against <¤Cband.name> is quite the opposite of what the band had in mind when they hired you as their manager.\n\tThe band gives up the hopeless fight and go back to living lives far from the show-biz frenzy.

<¤Crealmusician.name> leaving <¤Cband.name> was the last stroke of bad luck.\n\tThe rest of the band decide it's time to realise that they don't have what it takes to compete in a world like this.\n\tIt's better they stop pretending and go back to their old day jobs at LardBurger.
You should try to keep the band together.\n\tThey can probably survive one person leaving the band, but two is too many.\n\tTry again and spend more time taking care of your artists.
